item.title: ZLMediaKit vs SRS vs Ant Media Server in 2026: Which Low-Latency Streaming Server Actually Survives Production?
item.description: You pointed OBS at a server, hit “Start Streaming”, and the preview in the browser arrived 8 seconds late. That is not a bug in OBS, your browser, or your network — it is HLS doing exactly what HLS does. If your users expect to watch a referee decision, a lecture, or a security camera without narrating the past, you need a streaming server built around an ingest protocol and a low-latency delivery path, not a segment-based one.

item.title: Self-Hosted Streaming Media Servers: SRS vs OvenMediaEngine vs Node-Media-Server
item.description:
Introduction

Live streaming infrastructure has evolved dramatically beyond simple RTMP relays. Modern streaming servers now support sub-second latency with WebRTC and SRT protocols, adaptive bitrate transcoding, and massive-scale viewer distribution — all from a self-hosted deployment. Whether you’re building a live video platform, a surveillance camera aggregator, or a low-latency broadcast pipeline, choosing the right media server is critical.
